findings.title: Check 35 rule 6 is red on this batch's own ledger commit; it landed only because no commit-time loop runs the rule
findings.evidence: Disposable worktree at fd2f7ca, a460628's ledger staged (git show a460628:.beads/issues.jsonl > new file; mv; git add), then python3 lint/checks/35-board-integrity.py -> rc=1: 'closed bead ac-4y7l.11 / .12 / .13 / .4 carries no landing record is RED'. Those four were closed through the gate between 07:31 and 07:38Z, before 07c3cf5 (07:48Z) taught the gate to write a record. The coordinator ledger commit that carried them came after the rule existed. It landed anyway because .git/hooks/pre-commit in this checkout runs gitleaks only (round 1 recorded this, and it is still true), and coordinator.sh -> swarm-commit.sh never runs lint.sh --changed. Plan A1 ('land the rule and the record together so the rule never turns red') assumed ledger commits happen per close. In practice a run batches every close of the run into one ledger commit at close-out, so any close made before the record code ships is judged as new. The rule's only proven loop is its own fixture suite.
findings.fix: Put rule 6 on a real commit-time path: have coordinator.sh (or swarm-commit.sh's ledger leg) run lint/checks/35-board-integrity.py against the staged ledger before it commits, or install the hooks.d chain in this checkout. Add a cutover guard, like rule 3's origin cutover, so closes with closed_at before the rule's landing are never judged. Backfill a note on ac-4y7l.4/.11/.12/.13, or record that they closed pre-rule.

findings.title: RECORD-FAILED exits 1 after the close has landed, colliding with CLOSE-REFUSED's 'bead stays open' contract
findings.evidence: close-gate.sh:200 and :603 print RECORD-FAILED and exit 1 after `br close` has already succeeded. The gate's header says 'Exit 1 CLOSE-REFUSED — a named leg failed; the bead stays open'. worker.md §7 maps exit 1 to 'Fix what the leg names and re-run'; §8 maps it to 'comment, unclaim, §1'. rg -n RECORD-FAILED across skills/ finds no consumer outside close-gate.sh. A worker that gets RECORD-FAILED therefore treats a CLOSED bead as open and re-runs or unclaims it. The bead stays closed with no record, and rule 6 then refuses the next ledger commit (see finding 1). br 0.5.12's `br close --transition-comment <COMMENT>` ('New comment committed atomically with each close transition', per `br close --help`) would remove the post-close window entirely.
findings.fix: Write the landing record atomically: `"$BR" close "$BEAD" --reason "$REASON" --transition-comment "$LND_TEXT"`, with LND_TEXT computed before the close. If the two-step write is kept, give RECORD-FAILED its own exit code (for example 3), document it in the header, and add a worker.md §7/§8 arm: 'closed; re-add the record with br comments add, never re-run the gate'.

findings.title: Org-wide docket sweep sources br-call.sh from the cwd repo's skills/, so from ~/mission or 3 of 4 apps every repo renders DEGRADED
findings.evidence: The sweep sources `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/skills/_tools/br-call.sh`. That path exists only in agent-compounds and body-compass-app (where skills is an untracked symlink to .agents/skills). art-still-app, unsit-app, move-free-app and ~/mission have no skills/ dir. Reproduced the snippet verbatim from cwd ~/mission with REPOS_ROOT=~/mission/software and APPS_LIST={art-still-app, agent-compounds}. Output: 'br-call.sh: No such file or directory', 'br_call: command not found', then 'DEGRADED .../art-still-app' and 'DEGRADED .../agent-compounds'. From the agent-compounds root the same loop reads 24/51/102 rows fine. The sensor meant to make 'silence means clean' now alarms on every repo at org level, which is the sweep's stated use ('At org level or asked across everything'). The same repo-relative class sits in action-loop.md:20 and human-gate-template.md: `skills/ac-implement/scripts/close-gate.sh <id>` does not exist in art-still/unsit/move-free, so the ruling close there fails 'No such file'.
findings.fix: Resolve the helper from the skill's own install, never from the cwd repo. For example, `. "$HOME/mission/software/agent-compounds/skills/_tools/br-call.sh"`, or the `.claude/skills/_tools/br-call.sh` symlink every deploy target carries (verified present in all apps). Refuse once, loudly, if sourcing fails, instead of degrading per repo. Use the same resolvable path for close-gate.sh in action-loop.md and human-gate-template.md.

findings.title: touchers.test.sh Case 12 red: caused by 07c3cf5 (ac-4y7l.5) adding 5 close-gate referrers without re-deriving bead-schema.md's example count
findings.evidence: bash skills/_tools/touchers.test.sh -> 'FAIL: Case 12 ... touchers for skills/ac-implement/scripts/close-gate.sh declare → 8 but the command reproduces 13'. I ran git grep -l -F 'scripts/close-gate' over the rg exclusion set at each commit, dropping the 5 .claude/ hits that rg's hidden-dir default skips. Result: 2dc960b = 8, 07c3cf5 = 13. The +5 are all added by 07c3cf5: lint/checks/35-board-integrity.py, skills/ac-human/references/action-loop.md, skills/beads-standards/SKILL.md, skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md, skills/beads-standards/reference/human-gate-template.md. So the cause is confirmed: ac-4y7l.5's close gate ran per-bead probes only, and Case 12 judges a worked example against the live tree, so any new referrer anywhere turns it red.
findings.fix: Re-derive the example line to → 13. Better, make Case 12 hermetic: run the example against a fixture tree, or only validate its shape and self-consistency, so the schema's teaching example stops being a live-repo count sensor that any unrelated doc edit can break.

findings.title: Rule 5 picks 'new' comments by position, but br orders comments by created_at, so a legacy receipt is still re-judged
findings.evidence: new_comments[rid] = staged_comments[len(head_comments):] assumes append order. The live ledger shows br exports comments sorted by created_at with nondeterministic same-second ties, not by id: ac-kqpw.5 [264,263], ac-gcj.8 [104,103], ac-1p7j.31 [1619,1620,1618]. Reproduced in a scratch repo: at HEAD, ac-legacy has one legacy receipt (created 10:05). Staged adds a note with created_at 10:01, so br's order puts it first. The check returns rc=1: 'malformed WORKER receipt is RED: bead ac-legacy comment WORKER: model=foo session=bar ...'. That is the exact wedge ac-4y7l.12 set out to remove. The bead's own fix said 'absent from the same row at HEAD' (a set difference). Every suite fixture appends at the tail, a shape that does not cover imported or same-second comments.
findings.fix: Compute new comments as a set difference by comment id: head_ids = {c['id'] for c in head_comments}; new = [c for c in staged_comments if c.get('id') not in head_ids]. Fall back to (created_at, text) when id is absent. Add a fixture where the new comment sorts before the legacy one.

findings.title: close-gate suite never asserts the GATE: receipt record or RECORD-FAILED: both survive sabotage
findings.evidence: grep -n 'GATE: receipt\|RECORD-FAILED' close-gate.test.sh -> no hits. In a disposable worktree at fd2f7ca I made two sabotages. (a) Set the receipt branch's LND_TEXT to 'note' -> close-gate.test.sh: all 58 case(s) passed. (b) Changed the record write to `br_call comments add ... || true` so RECORD-FAILED can never fire -> all 58 passed. ac-4y7l.5's spec requires 'a receipt-backed close records GATE: receipt'. The one landing branch every ordinary close takes, and its failure mode, are unguarded, while check 35 rule 6 depends on exactly that prefix.
findings.fix: In an existing receipt-backed accept case, assert that comments.log contains a line starting 'GATE: receipt — <bead>'. Add a case with a mock `comments add` that exits non-zero: assert the output contains RECORD-FAILED, the gate's exit code, and that the bead reads closed.

findings.title: Ruling path swallows a refused comments read as 'no ruling found' (exit 1) instead of NOT-CHECKED (exit 2)
findings.evidence: RULING=$(br_call comments list "$BEAD" --json 2>/dev/null | jq ... 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 ...). No return code is checked and stderr is discarded, which contradicts br-call.sh's own rule: 'never redirects a br read's stderr to /dev/null'. Probe: a fake AC2_BR_CMD returns a decision-type show and, for `comments`, the error envelope {"error":{"code":"DB_LOCKED"}} with exit 1. Running `close-gate.sh ac-d1 --reason 'decided: x' --dry-run` prints 'CLOSE-REFUSED DECISION: no DECISION (<actor>) comment found on ac-d1' with rc=1. A dead read is reported as a verified absence, which is the empty-is-not-clean failure br_call exists to stop, and a human is told to record a ruling that may already exist.
findings.fix: Split the read from the match: `CMTS=$(br_call comments list "$BEAD" --json </dev/null) || not_checked "READ" "comments list refused for $BEAD"`, then run jq -e over the array (refuse NOT-CHECKED on a non-array shape), then grep. Add a suite case with a failing comments list that expects exit 2.
